Outputs are editable vector graphics (SVG/PDF), and free daily credits let researchers try before paying. Used by researchers at institutions including Harvard, MIT, and Stanford.

figma-ai.verdict: Figma's native AI layer: a canvas agent, prompt-to-prototype Make, and model workflows built into the design platform on a shared AI-credit system.
overview: Figma AI is a suite of AI capabilities built natively into the Figma platform rather than sold as a standalone product. Per Figma's official AI page, it centers on three workflows — Explore, Polish, Ship — including the Figma agent, Figma Make for turning prompts into prototypes and web apps, Weave model workflows, generative plugins, visual search, and MCP server integration. AI usage runs on shared monthly AI credits included with each seat (500 on Starter up to 4,250 on Enterprise Full seats), with paid credit top-ups available.
features: Figma agent (beta) — generates design directions, edits images, automates busywork on canvas
Figma Make — prompts turn ideas and existing designs into prototypes and web apps
Make on local codebase (beta) — converts designs into localized, production-ready assets
Weave tools (beta) — pre-built AI workflows generating images and vectors in Figma
Generative plugins — prompt reusable custom plugins right on the canvas
Text tools and design productivity tools — rewrite content, adjust tone, rename layers, add interactions
Visual search — find components and assets with AI
MCP server — connects Figma designs to external agentic tools
pros: Deep native integration: works inside the design platform teams already use, aware of design systems and components
Make produces editable prototypes and can push back to a codebase via pull requests
Credit allowances scale with plan and seat type; agent is free during beta
cons: Suite is fragmented across Agent, Make, Weave, and Dev Mode surfaces with no single entry point
Credits burn fast and don't roll over; heavy use requires a higher-tier seat or paid top-ups
Several headline features sit in closed beta or waitlists, and AI requires the Figma ecosystem

figr.verdict: AI product design agent that learns your live product and generates on-brand UX flows and prototypes.
overview: Figr is an AI design agent for product teams that learns your existing product before generating new work. It ingests Figma files or captures your live product through a Chrome extension, then builds context-aware flows, edge cases and high-fidelity prototypes that respect your design system. It maps flows, flags edge cases and explains UX tradeoffs so the first design review is already grounded.
features: Live product capture via Chrome extension
Figma file import with components, variants and tokens
High-fidelity prototype generation in your design system
Flow and edge-case mapping before design
UX decision review with tradeoff explanations
Selective element editing without full regeneration
pros: Designs match your existing product instead of generic templates
Thinks through flows and edge cases before producing screens
Selective edits keep the rest of the design intact
cons: Built for existing products, less suited to blank-canvas design
Quality depends on the context you feed it
Relatively new product with an evolving feature set

fill-3d.verdict: AI that virtually stages rooms from a text prompt using 3D-aware path tracing.
overview: Fill 3D is an experimental AI tool that virtually stages a room using only a text prompt. Instead of 2D inpainting, it reconstructs the scene in 3D and renders additions with path tracing for realistic lighting and shadows. The project was built on the Function (fxn.ai) GPU compute platform and is aimed at real-estate media and virtual staging workflows.
pros: Physically realistic results via 3D path tracing
cons: Early beta with reduced output resolution
Limited to room staging use cases
No public pricing or production API details

findmine.verdict: AI outfitting platform that automatically builds shoppable complete-the-look recommendations for fashion retailers.
overview: FindMine generates AI-curated outfits and 'complete the look' recommendations that plug into retailers' product pages, emails, and ads. Its engines style full looks from a brand's own catalog at scale, increasing basket size without manual merchandising. Clients include major apparel brands such as Lululemon and Gap.
pros: Trusted by major brands like Lululemon and Gap
cons: Retailer-facing only
Pricing not public
Needs large catalog to shine

fit-analytics.verdict: Machine-learning size recommendation platform for apparel brands, built on two decades of fit and returns data.
overview: Fit Analytics is a machine-learning platform that predicts the right size for every shopper using order and return data from leading apparel brands. After years as part of Snap, the team reclaimed independence and now builds toward AI-powered shopping assistants alongside its core size engine. Its models learn from two decades of fit data to reduce size-related returns.
pros: Two decades of fit training data
Proven results with large European retailers
cons: B2B only — no consumer app
Recently independent, strategy in transition
Integration requires developer resources

fit-match.verdict: LiDAR-powered 3D body-shape fit matching that pairs shoppers with a digital twin instead of measurements.
overview: Fit:match solves fit with a patented 3D shape-based approach instead of measurements: shoppers complete a LiDAR body scan in seconds, then get matched to a 'digital twin' with a similar body shape who has already tried the product. It launched bra fitting in select Macy's stores and now also powers an app matching post-surgery patients with compression garments. The method ignores measurements entirely, relying on 3D body shape data.
cons: Primarily in-store experience
Bra category focus initially
Requires LiDAR-enabled device
